title: The Clockmaker's Last Hour
theme: Every clock stopped the moment the clockmaker vanished.
description: Rebuild a broken gear train, wake the workshop's clocks, and set the hour the clockmaker left.
intro: The clockmaker vanished at the stroke of an hour no one remembers, and every clock in his workshop stopped with him. Dust hangs in the air like a held breath. The door has no keyhole at all, only a brass bolt wired to a towering grandfather clock.

clues.diary: The clockmaker's diary: "I stopped every clock at the very moment my cuckoo first sang tonight, a quarter past the hour."
clues.cuckoo: The cuckoo burst out and sang seven times, exactly, before sulking back inside.

inspect.title: The door
say: The bolt hangs loose. You pull the door open, and the workshop exhales.

inspect.title: The door
say: No keyhole, no handle, only a heavy brass bolt. A thin wire runs from it across the ceiling to the grandfather clock.
Under a tangle of springs and tiny screws: a great iron wheel, heavy as a held breath, its teeth still bright with oil.
Springs, screws, and the smell of oil. Nothing else of use.

inspect.title: The gear train
say: Every wheel turns in time now, ticking like a heartbeat. Up on the wall, the cuckoo clock stirs.

inspect.title: The gear train
say: The little gear sits snugly on its axle. A great empty axle still waits beside it.

inspect.title: The gear train
say: The great wheel sits heavy on its axle. A small empty axle still waits beside it.

inspect.title: The gear train
say: The heart of the workshop: a train of wheels with two empty axles, one small and one large. Without them, every clock here is dead.

rules.title: The gear train
say: The little gear slips on. The wheels catch, shudder, and begin to turn! Above you, a cuckoo clock clears its throat.

rules.title: The gear train
say: The little gear slips onto the small axle with a satisfying click. It still needs its larger partner.

rules.title: The gear train
say: The great wheel drops into place. The wheels catch, shudder, and begin to turn! Above you, a cuckoo clock clears its throat.

rules.title: The gear train
say: The great wheel settles onto the large axle with a deep clunk. It still needs a smaller partner.
The little door snaps open and the cuckoo bursts out, singing seven times exactly, then sulks back inside.
A carved cuckoo clock, its little door shut tight. Its pendulum hangs dead still.
Tools lie exactly where the clockmaker dropped them. His diary lies open: "I stopped every clock at the very moment my cuckoo first sang tonight, a quarter past the hour."
Beside it, a little brass gear.
The diary lies open: "I stopped every clock at the very moment my cuckoo first sang tonight, a quarter past the hour."
Its hands rest at a quarter past seven. The wire to the door hangs slack.
A tall grandfather clock, ticking again at last. Its hands turn freely now. A wire runs from its case to the door's bolt.
A tall grandfather clock, frozen. Its hands won't budge, as if the whole workshop has stopped breathing.

lock.title: The grandfather clock
lock.prompt: Set the hour hand and the minute hand.

solved.title: The grandfather clock
say: You set the hands to a quarter past seven. The clock chimes once, low and certain, and the wire to the door goes slack: the bolt is drawn.

wrong: The clock ticks disapprovingly. Not that hour.
A hollow chime. The clockmaker never left at that time.
The hands shiver and slip back to where they were.

levels: Every clock here has stopped. What makes a clock go?
The gear train has two empty axles, one small and one large. Both missing pieces are somewhere in the workshop.
Take the little gear from the workbench and the great wheel from the toolbox, then use both on the gear train.
Now that things are moving, listen to the clocks.
The diary on the workbench says when the clockmaker stopped the clocks. The cuckoo clock tells you the hour.
The cuckoo sings seven times, and the diary says a quarter past. Set the grandfather clock to 7:15.
The door's bolt was wired to the grandfather clock.
Listen: the bolt has been drawn.
Click the door to leave the workshop.

wrongItemLine: That doesn't fit anywhere here. The clockmaker would have tutted.
escapeText: The bolt slides back, the door creaks open, and behind you every clock in the workshop begins to tick again, as if to say goodbye.
